title: Prime Henkin theories for equality-free intuitionistic first-order logic
summary: Extend a supported nonconsequence to a prime theory with named existential witnesses, preserving an infinite reserve for future counterinstances.
abstract: A first-order world that accepts an existential assertion needs an object witnessing it. An implication or universal assertion must also remain valid when the world acquires more information and more objects. We construct equality-free intuitionistic theories with these two needs in mind: disjunctions select a disjunct, existentials receive a present parameter witness, and omitted implications or universals have counterexamples in larger theories. The construction preserves any given supported nonconsequence in a countable language while keeping infinitely many parameter names unused. This supplies the syntactic worlds and extension properties needed for varying-domain Kripke completeness.
